items.title: 3 unexpected reasons the October jobs report was so strong
items.summary: October's jobs report blew past economist forecasts. Here are three reasons.
items.body: A little-noticed category in Friday's blockbuster jobs report is challenging the consensus view about job losses caused by artificial intelligence. At least for now, the data suggests the U.S. is gaining jobs as a result of the AI boom, not losing them. And another category suggests the strong jobs numbers could have some staying power. Nonfarm payrolls grew by 165,000 jobs in October, according to the Friday report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It was a surprising surge in hiring that blew way past Wall Street's expectations. Economists polled by Dow Jones had forecast growth of just 59,000 for the month. Hiring for consultants surged in the month, sending the profession's total head count to a fresh record.

items.title: Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance
items.summary: Securitize saw growth in tokenization last quarter and announced its expansion into asset-backed finance through the acquisition of River One.
items.body: Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition. Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year. The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.

items.title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.summary: The share price dropped wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the value of Nvidia.
items.body: Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair. Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China. However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".

items.title: Silicon Valley and Trump rally behind Nvidia CEO after his affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.summary: Elon Musk and other finance moguls defend Jensen Huang after he admitted to the affair in an email to employees Nvidia’s board needs to do some succession planning – sharpish Donald Trump , Elon Musk and prominent finance moguls have expressed their support for embattled Nvidia…
items.body: Donald Trump , Elon Musk and prominent finance moguls have expressed their support for embattled Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , as the head of the world’s most valuable chip company faces an internal investigation over a romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. “I have not ​spoken to him about it,” the US president told reporters on Sunday. “I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what is going on. I’m sure, I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job”. “I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it,” Trump later added, saying he believed that Huang would and should stay on as CEO. Huang’s defenders framed his affair as a personal lapse in judgment rather than evidence of treachery against the United States, which has imposed strict limits on what chips Nvidia can sell to China.

items.title: China sets plans for yuan use in shipping risk-pricing, curbing reliance on West
items.summary: China has unveiled a road map to strengthen its maritime insurance industry and expand the use of the yuan in shipping-related transactions, as Beijing seeks to reduce its reliance on Western-dominated insurance networks amid growing geopolitical tensions. The guidelines,…
items.body: China has unveiled a road map to strengthen its maritime insurance industry and expand the use of the yuan in shipping-related transactions, as Beijing seeks to reduce its reliance on Western-dominated insurance networks amid growing geopolitical tensions. The guidelines, jointly issued by seven government agencies on Friday, aim to strengthen domestic underwriting and risk-pricing capabilities while expanding insurance protection for China’s key imports and exports. The push comes as Western sanctions on Russian oil shipments and disruptions to global commodity trade and shipping caused by the war in Iran have highlighted the strategic importance of maritime insurance, a sector in which Western insurers, particularly those based in London, remain dominant.

items.title: Nvidia stock falls 4% as scrutiny turns to Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy
items.summary: Nvidia said its board has launched an independent investigation following the reports that Huang was the target of a "foreign intelligence effort."
items.body: Nvidia stock closed 4.27% lower on Monday after the tech giant launched an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy. U.S. intelligence agencies said Alice Huang, an executive at cloud company Megaspeed, has been passing information to Beijing, according to reports in The New York Times and the Financial Times . Nvidia said its board has launched an independent investigation following the reports that Huang was the target of a "foreign intelligence effort." Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," the company said in a Sunday statement . The co-founder and CEO told staff in an email that he had "fallen short" of his responsibility to serve his colleagues, the board, partners and shareholders around the world. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children.

items.title: A key report for where inflation stood in October comes out Tuesday. Here's what to expect
items.summary: The CPI headline reading is expected to show an increase of 0.3% while the core is forecast to increase 0.2%.
items.body: Falling gasoline prices provided some relief to consumers in October, but Federal Reserve officials are increasingly concerned that inflation pressures elsewhere in the economy are proving harder to contain. Prices at the pump declined by more than 4%, according to the Energy Information Administration, providing a respite from a surge that had added more than a dollar a gallon over the past year. However, the consumer price index for the month, which the Bureau of Labor Statistics will release Tuesday at 8:30 a.m., is expected to show only a slight let-up. Meanwhile, Fed officials say they are worried that inflation initially driven higher by President Donald Trump 's tariffs and the Iran war is proving more persistent than expected, with price pressures emerging in sectors beyond those directly affected by the shocks.

items.title: A massive trade in Nvidia just went off – here are the details
items.summary: Despite Monday's sell-off, options traders are targeting new highs on Nvidia
items.body: The biggest options trade on Nvidia stock Monday seems to think the controversy swirling around the chip leader and its embattled CEO is creating a buying opportunity. In a trade about an hour after the opening bell that involved more than $100 million in options premium, someone exchanged an existing call spread for a more bullish position that captures the next five months of trading in Nvidia. The core position was the purchase of 52,000 195-strike calls expiring Feb. 19 worth about $57 million – contracts the trader opened for a new long position while simultaneously selling the same number of 245-strike calls for the same expiry, lowering the cost of the trade by $10 million. The net position, a bullish call spread, needs Nvidia to trade above around $206 by expiry, or about 15% higher, to be profitable.

items.title: Zoe Kleinman: Nvidia CEO's affair will cause ripples across US and beyond
items.summary: Jensen Huang is being investigated by his own company over an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy.
items.body: The tech world has spent the day digesting the extraordinary news that Jensen Huang - the charismatic, leather-jacket wearing chief executive of the multi-trillion dollar firm Nvidia - is being investigated by his own company over an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Huang's alleged romantic affair with Alice Huang (no relation), the former CEO of a Singapore-based data centre company, has cast ripples far beyond his immediate family - undoubtedly on an emotional rollercoaster of their own - taking us to a crossroads at which technology, geopolitics and national security intersect. In a nutshell, this is about the bitter rivalry between the US and China, as well as whether Jensen Huang has betrayed the US as well as his wife. "Whoever wins AI, wins," as US President Donald Trump puts it.

items.title: Boeing to cut about 5% of its commercial plane workforce
items.summary: Company will cut jobs through a mix of layoffs and attrition as it moderates the pace of ramping up jet production Boeing will cut about 5% of its commercial plane workforce as it moderates the pace of ramping up jet production, the company said on Monday. The company will…
items.body: Boeing will cut about 5% of its commercial plane workforce as it moderates the pace of ramping up jet production, the company said on Monday. The company will eliminate the posts through a mix of layoffs and attrition because of a slower ramp-up to “provide our factories and supply chain partners additional time to achieve stability”, said a message to employees from Boeing commercial chief Stephanie Pope. “Adjusting our production schedules and reducing aircraft output puts us in an overstaffed position,” she added. Pope praised the team for improved operations reflected in US certifications this year of the 737 Max 7 and 737 Max 10. “While we have made substantial progress, we have not yet fully recovered,” said Pope, who promised to treat employees with “dignity and respect” as the company moves ahead with layoff notifications beginning in December.

items.title: Hegseth impeachment articles introduced by Rep. Massie
items.summary: The House is likely to vote this week on articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth filed by Republican Rep. Thomas Masie.
items.body: Rep. Thomas Massie , R-Ky., on Monday introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth , triggering a vote in the House of Representatives as early as this week. The unusual impeachment push against Hegseth by a member of his own party comes after Democrats swept to majorities in both the House and Senate during last week's midterm elections . Many Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance , have cited the Iran war Hegseth has led as a reason for the electoral bludgeoning. Massie, who lost his reelection bid in a Republican primary in May, introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth. They include waging war in contravention of war powers resolutions Congress passed to limit war, extrajudicial killings tied to boat strikes in the Caribbean that purported to target drug smugglers and suppressing free speech by targeting Sen.

items.title: China wholesale inflation hits highest in more than four years as consumer measure slows
items.summary: The PPI for October came in at 5.7%, compared to the 5.3% expected by economists polled by Reuters.
items.body: Producer prices in China grew at the fastest rate since June 2022, accelerating for the third month in a row. The PPI for October came in at 5.7%, compared to the 5.3% expected by economists polled by Reuters. The increase was driven by a sharp rise in prices in the mining and raw materials industries. The increase was driven by very strong external demand, Zhang Zhiwei, president and chief economist at Pinpoint Asset Management, told CNBC's " Squawk Box Asia ." Consumer inflation in China slowed to 0.7% in October, its first deceleration after two straight months of increases. The figure missed expectations of a 0.8% rise from economists polled by Reuters, and was lower than the 0.9% seen in September. Core inflation, which strips out food and energy prices, came in at 0.8%, down from the 1% seen in the month before.

items.title: Millions of dollars poured into prediction markets on election night, trading on Democratic control of Congress and Texas governor's race
items.summary: Election night showed how traders reacted in real time to midterm results, as trading activity surged and market prices shifted to Democrats on Nov. 3.
items.body: More than 87% of all election markets across Kalshi and Polymarket gave the right candidate at least a 90% chance of winning their race 24 hours before election night, a CNBC analysis found. Election night showed how traders reacted to real-time midterm results, as trading activity surged and market prices shifted to Democrats after results from Indiana began rolling in before 7 p.m. on Nov. 3. Many midterm races were uncompetitive, which boosted the overall hit rate on prediction markets. "I'd say prediction markets did pretty well," said Koleman Strumpf, a professor of economics at Wake Forest University. "But they didn't outperform the best," he added, referring to traditional forecast polls that tracked results that night. Odds and gambling platforms do not use methodologies used by traditional political polling, and therefore are not substitutes for political polls. After 8 p.m.

items.title: Civil servant who secretly held five jobs found guilty of fraud
items.summary: Kashim Chowdhury had secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries.
items.body: A civil servant who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud. Kashim Chowdhury, from east London, had five government jobs that overlapped in the spring of 2023. He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money. The prosecution accused the 56-year-old of ''deliberate, intentional dishonesty'' and of ''exploiting the system''. After seven hours of deliberation, the jury unanimously found Chowdhury guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by a failure to disclose. The judge said Chowdhury faced a ''very significant custodial sentence''. He added he was refusing bail because of the significance of the crime and for Chowdhury's own wellbeing.

items.title: EU sues IBM and two European firms over troubled entry/exit border system
items.summary: Lawsuit filed last year against IBM, Atos and Leonardo after delays to delivery to troubled new system The EU has filed a lawsuit against IBM and two other companies involved in its troubled border-management system, an internal document has revealed. The bloc’s IT agency,…
items.body: The EU has filed a lawsuit against IBM and two other companies involved in its troubled border-management system, an internal document has revealed. The bloc’s IT agency, EU-Lisa, filed a case last year against IBM, the French IT company Atos and Italian defence contractor Leonardo, the three members of a consortium to implement and maintain the EU’s entry/exit system , which was launched in October 2025. The rollout has faced significant difficulties: some passengers at peak times have missed their flights as a result of delays blamed on the new technology and a lack of staff at the border. The agency’s decision to sue the companies was revealed in its latest annual accounts, which stated that “following the various delays in the delivery of the EES by a contracting consortium the agency activated the available contractual and legal remedies to protect its financial interest”.

items.title: China’s tax compliance drive falls short of covering fiscal gaps, weighs on sentiment: report
items.summary: Even as China’s stricter enforcement lifts tax receipts, the revenue gains remain insufficient to cover government funding gaps and risk chilling private sector confidence, while local officials remain reluctant to launch major projects despite repeated calls from Beijing,…
items.body: Even as China’s stricter enforcement lifts tax receipts, the revenue gains remain insufficient to cover government funding gaps and risk chilling private sector confidence, while local officials remain reluctant to launch major projects despite repeated calls from Beijing, analysts say. Hong Kong-based Goldman Sachs analysts, led by Wang Lisheng, estimated in a Monday report that tighter tax enforcement may have added roughly 500 billion yuan (US$74.91 billion) to mainland China’s government coffers this year compared with 2021 – before the prolonged property slump and Covid lockdowns. Of that total, 300 billion yuan came from tax revenue and 200 billion yuan from social security contributions. Even so, the effort still fell “well short” of plugging the government’s funding gap, the report noted.

items.title: PepsiCo to cut about 1,000 jobs as North American business struggles
items.summary: PepsiCo plans to cut about 1,000 jobs across North America as it streamlines operations and works to revive sales in its home market.
items.body: PepsiCo is cutting about 1,000 jobs across North America as the company tries to turn around lagging sales in its home market. "We have a clear ambition for PepsiCo North America: to build a stronger, more future-fit business that delivers industry-leading growth," Ram Krishnan, CEO of PepsiCo North America, wrote in a Monday letter to employees obtained by CNBC. "To do that, we need to be faster, more connected, and more capable, while continuing to invest in growth – behind our people, capabilities and brands." Over the next week, Pepsi plans to cut jobs as it says it aims to streamline its operations and better connect teams across the company's North American business. PepsiCo employs about 306,000 people worldwide, including roughly 125,000 in the United States, as of Dec. 27, according to a company filing.

items.title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long
items.summary: Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of fraud after pocketing £284,000 of taxpayers' money over three years.
items.body: He'd been on sick leave from his job at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for nearly three months and Adams, his line manager, wanted to put a plan in action to ease him back into work. At the start of the call, Chowdhury was coughing and waving tissues up to the camera in an attempt to show how ill he was. But what really caught Adams' attention was how pale he looked. She noticed white powder had started separating from his forehead. "He was sweating, it was like rubbing off, so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck," she told his trial. She claimed he was wearing white make-up to look sick. Something he denied in court. That month, he was also being paid to work full-time for the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office.

items.title: Thames Water asks creditors for more time to help repay £20bn debt pile
items.summary: Troubled utility lobbies for deadline on part of the debt to be extended to March 2028 Thames Water has asked creditors for more time to pay back billions of pounds in debt, as the water company scrambles to keep itself afloat. The UK’s largest water company said it had proposed…
items.body: Thames Water has asked creditors for more time to pay back billions of pounds in debt, as the water company scrambles to keep itself afloat. The UK’s largest water company said it had proposed an “interim” deal under which the deadline to pay off an unspecified portion of the £20bn of debt on its balance sheet would be extended from 2027 to March 2028. The company, which serves 16 million customers across London and the Thames Valley, has been on the brink of collapse for several years after it became overwhelmed by debt. Its shareholders walked away in 2024, which in effect left the company under the control of its creditors, who are working out a deal to avoid bankruptcy. The creditors gave Thames Water a separate £3bn lifeline in February last year to try to see it through negotiations on a deal to reduce its debts and inject more money.

items.title: China’s factory gate inflation accelerates in October with highest increase since 2022
items.summary: China’s factory-gate price growth continued to accelerate last month amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict that is fuelling uncertainties in the global energy market, while consumer inflation remained subdued. The producer price index (PPI) rose 5.7 per cent year on year in October,…
items.body: China’s factory-gate price growth continued to accelerate last month amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict that is fuelling uncertainties in the global energy market, while consumer inflation remained subdued. The producer price index (PPI) rose 5.7 per cent year on year in October, according to data released by the National Bureau of Statistics on Monday. It marked another record high since mid-2022, following a 5 per cent rise in September. The reading beat a projection of 5.37 per cent from economists polled by financial data provider Wind. China’s consumer price index, another major gauge of inflation, rose 0.7 per cent year on year in October, compared with 0.9 per cent in September. Wind projected a 0.83 per cent rise.

items.title: Skydance outlines its $6 billion in planned cost savings. Here's the breakdown

items.body: Skydance is pulling back the curtain on how it plans to achieve at least $6 billion in cost savings in the next three years. "By combining two global streaming services, two film and TV studio groups, two television portfolios, and overlapping corporate functions, we can reduce duplicative spend across an expense base of more than $50 billion," the company wrote in a letter to shareholders Monday as part of Paramount Skydance's third-quarter earnings release. Skydance, the newly formed combination of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, said it projects at least $2.2 billion in cost reductions from eliminating "redundant back-office and corporate functions," including eliminating management layers and ramping the use of artificial intelligence. Those savings also account for "rationalizing" its office footprint.

items.title: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
items.summary: The discount chain is continuing to edge towards collapse and is said to be "running on fumes", according to one insider.
items.body: Poundland is unable to buy new stock to fill its shelves after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts. The discount chain is on the brink of collapse with one insider describing it as "running on fumes". It has until Thursday to secure a rescue deal. About £50m has been frozen by its American owner Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning its 600 shops are running out of stock. Pressure is building on Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for £1 last June, after the owner rejected a takeover bid that could have saved the thousands of jobs currently at risk. Gordon Brothers has been approached for comment. Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its creditors until Thursday.

items.title: High fossil fuel prices spread inflation ‘like a cancer’, UN climate chief tells Cop31
items.summary: Simon Stiell makes opening address at summit in Turkey, where talks are under way about speeding up shift to electrification A global fossil fuel price crisis is “spreading inflation like a cancer” around the planet, the UN’s climate chief, Simon Stiell, told the opening plenary…
items.body: A global fossil fuel price crisis is “spreading inflation like a cancer” around the planet, the UN’s climate chief, Simon Stiell, told the opening plenary of critical UN climate talks in Turkey . Stiell joined Cop31 hosts Turkey and Australia, which is leading the negotiations, in promoting renewable energy and a new electrification goal as an optimistic alternative to a planet still tied to oil, coal and gas. Inside the tight security of the opening plenary on Monday, delegates from almost 200 countries watched a stirring short film with scenes of fire, flood and storms that proclaimed: “It’s time to reconnect with the planet we have grown apart from.” Turkey said it expected 100,000 visitors, including national delegations, to attend the two-week talks, including at least 95 heads of state. A global leaders summit is scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday.

items.title: Lucid misses Wall Street’s earnings expectations, expands loan from Saudi Arabia fund

items.body: Lucid Group missed Wall Street's third-quarter expectations as the embattled electric vehicle maker continues an "operational reset" aimed at cutting costs and narrowing losses. The company on Monday also announced a $1.75 billion increase in a delayed draw term loan from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, the company's largest shareholder. Despite the top- and bottom-line misses, the company's adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of a loss $726 million beat Wall Street's expectations of a loss of $611 million for the third quarter. Its net loss for the quarter was $830.9 million, down from a loss of $978.4 million a year earlier. Lucid's 2025 third quarter included revenue of $336.6 million, a loss of $3.31 per share and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $717.7 million.

items.summary: The billionaire tech executive finds himself mired in a personal and national security scandal.
items.body: One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, prompting an investigation. US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing , according to a New York Times report. On Sunday, Huang admitted , external to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children. US tech giant Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the reports. The firm said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Huang was committed to continuing to lead the company.

items.title: ‘Obvious risk of further tragedy’ at rail crossing type at which Amazon driver died, inquiry finds
items.summary: Call for overhaul of manually operated level crossings after delivery worker was killed by passenger train in Kent An Amazon delivery driver was killed by a train after he drove his van on to railway tracks at a manually operated level crossing, apparently without realising he…
items.body: An Amazon delivery driver was killed by a train after he drove his van on to railway tracks at a manually operated level crossing, apparently without realising he needed to open the exit gate first, an official investigation has reported. Safety inspectors said there was “an obvious risk of further tragedy”, with a second similar fatal event still being investigated, and called for an overhaul of this type of crossing. The van driver, Brandon Hatcher, 23, of Ashford, Kent , died at the Bax crossing near Teynham after being hit by a passenger train from Ramsgate to London in July last year.

items.title: Rubio sees little hope of diplomatic breakthrough to Mideast deadlock amid 'outrageous' Iranian demands
items.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters that Iran negotiations remain unproductive.
items.body: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has accused Iran of "outrageous and ridiculous" demands as efforts to reach a lasting resolution in the Middle East war appeared stalled. Speaking with reporters in Florida on Sunday evening before traveling to Paris for the G7 foreign ministers' meeting, Rubio indicated the two sides remain far apart on negotiations, after Tehran proposed shortening the timetable for restarting talks from seven days to two. Rubio said President Donald Trump would prefer to solve "this and every problem diplomatically," but added that "sometimes that's not possible, unfortunately." Energy prices moved lower on Monday morning after President Trump said Sunday that further strikes were "highly unlikely" if negotiations progressed toward a strong agreement. Brent crude , the international price benchmark, was down 0.75% at $97.58 per barrel by 5:25 a.m. ET.

items.title: Doing these things now will help you save money at Christmas
items.summary: Small decisions made now can make a big difference to your festive finances, charities say, so here are some tips.
items.body: How soon is too soon when it comes to thinking about Christmas and your finances? The answer, of course, is that it is never too soon. Save early and the cost becomes more manageable. The squeeze is harder for some than others, with charity Barnardo's warning that some parents will skip meals so their kids get a Christmas dinner with the trimmings. But, debt advice charity StepChange is offering tips to everyone, to avoid Christmas spending leading to a financially painful new year. The best way to avoid a difficult January, it says, is to make a realistic plan before the spending begins. Stocktake before the big food shop . Check your cupboards, fridge and freezer before you go shopping and plan meals around food you already have. Make a list of what you need and compare prices. Think twice .

items.summary: Ministers pushed to reverse ‘policy madness’ of scrapping exemption on 5% tax rise for heat pumps, solar panels and batteries Households planning to invest in green energy upgrades, including heat pumps and solar panels, risk a nationwide rush to find an installer or face…
items.body: Households planning to invest in green energy upgrades, including heat pumps and solar panels, risk a nationwide rush to find an installer or face hundreds of pounds in unexpected costs unless the government abandons its looming VAT increase. Ministers are under growing pressure to reverse plans to scrap the 5% VAT exemption on home heat pumps, solar panels and batteries from 1 April which could add up to £1,530 on to the cost of a smart home energy system amid record demand for fossil fuel alternatives. Industry groups have warned that the VAT cliff-edge could trigger a surge in demand for installations before the deadline, creating a “feast and famine” upheaval for the country’s nascent network of home energy installers after years of tepid interest from households.

items.title: Could supplements be the next big opportunity in the GLP-1 weight-loss drug boom?
items.summary: Novonesis is exploring whether gut health supplements could benefit patients taking GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, opening up a potentially lucrative new market.
items.body: Supplements could be the next major sector to benefit from the weight-loss drug boom, Novonesis CEO told CNBC on Monday, as the biosolutions company explores whether microbiome products can help patients on popular GLP-1 medicines. "We have scientific evidence that [is] going to support the patients [on] GLP-1s feeling better, as a companion during the treatment," CEO Ester Baiget told "Squawk Box Europe," referencing an ongoing study with Novo Nordisk . GLP-1 medications and dietary supplements, such as those being developed by Novonesis, could play complementary roles in managing obesity and supporting longer-term health, she argued. While medications can help treat obesity, improving the gut microbiome through nutrition and scientifically backed supplements could support longer-term health, Baiget said.

items.body: One of the architects of Keir Stamer’s Brexit red lines has called for Andy Burnham to abandon them at the next election, saying a new relationship with the EU would protect the UK from global threats. The call is the latest voice from a prominent figure in Starmer’s administration for a faster transition to a far closer European relationship, after the former chancellor Rachel Reeves said it was right for Burnham to consider rejoining . Chris Ward, one of Starmer’s closest confidants in politics and one of the ministers who worked on the EU reset, said that it was the security relationship that meant a change was now imperative. The Labour MP for Brighton Kemptown and Peacehaven said it was now time to give a “a dignified retirement” to the red lines, which rule out rejoining the EU, the single market, the customs union and restoring freedom of movement .

items.summary: The launch comes as Anthropic is gearing up for what is widely expected to be a blockbuster IPO
items.body: Anthropic on Monday released two new artificial intelligence models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, as the company readies for a potentially historic IPO that could take place as soon as next week. Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are Anthropic's most advanced offerings, and the company said they generate outputs 30% faster than their predecessors. The models also cost 20% less than the 5.1 generation, and will be available for $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, the company said. The launch marks the first time that Anthropic has released so-called "frontier" models since its CEO, Dario Amodei , called to slow down the pace of AI development in September . Anthropic said the models went through rigorous safety and alignment testing, and that the company developed new evaluations and post-launch monitoring tools ahead of the release.

items.summary: New petrol or diesel cars are due to be phased out by 2030 and by 2035 all new cars must be zero emission.
items.body: The UK government's electric vehicle (EV) targets are expected to be reduced this week in a move likely to be welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups. Under the current rules, 80% of new cars sold in the UK must be electric by 2030 but industry groups have long called for "urgent relief". New petrol or diesel cars are due to be phased out by 2030 and by 2035 all new cars must be zero emission. But the speed of the transition to electric has been hotly debated, including within the cabinet. The government has been consulting on reducing its 80% rule and a significant reduction is now expected. A government source told the BBC it would approach the issue in a "pragmatic and balanced" way.

items.body: Fixing Britain’s youth jobs crisis will require ministers to drastically increase investment in employment support while avoiding arbitrary cuts to benefits, the head of the trade union movement has said. Before an important official report expected next week, the general secretary of the Trades Union Congress , Paul Nowak, said the government had a “once in a generation chance” to secure young people’s futures. In an interview with the Guardian before the highly anticipated Milburn review into young people and work, he said the costs of increasing job support, education and training would be outweighed by economic gains that would help to ease the pressure on the welfare state. “There is no solution that is cost-free,” he said.

items.body: Nvidia on Sunday said it has opened an investigation into co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman who intelligence agencies said is a Chinese spy . "Today's news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption," the company told CNBC in a statement. Below is a staff email from Huang obtained by CNBC and a statement released Sunday about the investigation from Nvidia's board of directors. The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation. The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.

Speaking to BBC Panorama, Miatta Fahnbulleh insisted that the government's drive for cleaner power would help to cut energy bills in the long term. But she conceded that the push to reduce carbon emissions was currently "under pressure" amid discontent at rising prices in recent years. It comes as ministers grapple with how to respond to a predicted surge in energy prices in January, expected to mark the biggest rise in bills for four years. Labour has faced extra political pressure over its climate ambitions since coming to power, as Reform UK rose in opinion polls and the Conservatives under Kemi Badenoch disowned their previous ambition of reaching net zero by 2050.

items.summary: The chipmaker faces business risks and political scrutiny due to its over-reliance on founder and CEO Jensen Huang Why is Nvidia’s Jensen Huang at the centre of a US-China row? Too big – and too well-connected – to sack? One doesn’t have to be overly cynical to think Jensen…
items.body: T oo big – and too well-connected – to sack? One doesn’t have to be overly cynical to think Jensen Huang, the Nvidia boss, starts with one huge advantage as the chipmaker’s board starts its independent investigation into the alleged honeytrap spy scandal . The world of US big tech is not, to put it mildly, strong on checks and balances on a founder’s power. Huang does not enjoy the supercharged voting rights that are par for the course elsewhere – his shareholding is a plain vanilla 3.6%. On the other hand, Nvidia’s board does not appear to have spent much time worrying about succession planning and “key person risk” or other standard concerns of corporate governance wonks outside the US. There isn’t even a Nvidia board member with the title of chair.

items.body: Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed is in the international spotlight after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, following reports linking him to Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. U.S. intelligence officials believe she is a Chinese intelligence asset, according to The New York Times. While the Nvidia CEO — one of the world's most prominent executives and a figurehead of the AI industry – did not name Megaspeed or Alice Huang in his statement, he acknowledged his infidelity and said Nvidia's Board of Directors had begun an independent investigation "regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports." "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American," he said.

items.title: Cyber-attack on French supermarket freezers has geopolitical context
items.summary: ‘Not particularly complex’ defrosting hack has been attributed to Iran, with presumption it is linked to others across Europe Iranian hackers like to send a message. In 2023 a state-backed group interrupted TV streaming services in the United Arab Emirates to broadcast a…
items.body: In 2023 a state-backed group interrupted TV streaming services in the United Arab Emirates to broadcast a deepfake report on the war in Gaza. In the same year, hackers affiliated with Iran displayed the slogan “down with Israel” on the screens of water-control equipment made by an Israeli firm. Now France has attributed an attack on supermarket fridges to hackers operating under the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, a key branch of Iran’s military establishment. There was no message this time, but the disruption made headlines around the world. Some refrigerators had their temperature turned up so high they caught fire. ‌In the hours after the hack, supermarket employees dumped piles of perished meat and melted ice-cream into rubbish containers.

items.body: Boeing said Monday that it plans to cut 5% of its commercial airplane workforce as its production ramp-up is moving at a slower pace than the company expected. The cuts will be through a combination of attrition and layoffs, Stephanie Pope, head of the commercial aircraft unit, said in a memo to staff. Pope reiterated that the company is still working to stabilize production rates of its bestselling 737 Max planes, which are made outside of Seattle. CEO Kelly Ortberg told investors last month that the company won't significantly increase production of the Max aircraft until the second half of next year. He said the company's wing production has been slower than expected. "Adjusting our production schedules and reducing aircraft output puts us in an overstaffed position," Pope said in her note Monday.

items.body: An off-grid hut that produces its own heating and electricity can continue to be the home of the man who built it, a council has decided. Geoffrey Finnimore, a self-employed architectural designer, erected the structure in Glandwr, near Crymych, in 2020, but never told authorities or asked for permission. Pembrokeshire council told him he must apply for retrospective permission for the home that is self-sufficient, and also collects rain water. However, the local authority found that because it has now been occupied as a home for more than four years, it is immune from prosecution action. "Without my home, which I created to solve my own problems and without state assistance, having to pay for other accommodation would be catastrophic for my finances and wellbeing," Finnimore said. The council asked him to apply for a lawful development certificate , external for the property.

items.title: How to get the buzz back on Britain’s high streets | Letters
items.summary: Readers respond to an article about the decline of town centres Sammy Gecsoyler’s report from Rotherham ( ‘It’s just vape shops, nail shops, charity shops’: can anything save the British high street?, 4 November ) tells the story in its dates. One out-of-town retail park in…
items.body: Sammy Gecsoyler’s report from Rotherham ( ‘It’s just vape shops, nail shops, charity shops’: can anything save the British high street?, 4 November ) tells the story in its dates. One out-of-town retail park in Britain in 1981; 385 by 1996. Parkgate opened in 1987 and MPs warned that it would disembowel towns and villages. It did. Rotherham town centre is now 24% vacant, while retail park vacancy nationally sits at 4.8%. That is not a mystery. It is 40 years of planning policy. We have since gone one step further by making home delivery cheaper than retail parks. Up to 3bn parcels a year now land on British doorsteps and not one of them passes through a town centre. Andy Burnham’s £210m for high streets is welcome, but is a one-off against a structural problem. What a town centre needs is a reason for people to walk into it again, every week, without being told to.

items.body: Applications for household grants of up to £250 are due to open for residents in part of Surrey. Tandridge District Council is funding the scheme, which last ran in January, to support residents with the cost of living . Applicants must live in the Tandridge district, be over 16 years old and be "experiencing financial hardship", the council says. They must also prove they are struggling to pay for essential items for themselves or their dependants by submitting full bank statements for August, September and October. Grants are available to households even if they receive support from elsewhere, such as Surrey County Council funds , external . items.title: The Guardian view on Jensen Huang’s affair: why did Trump ignore the warnings? | Editorial
items.summary: The AI chip boss’s actions raise urgent questions about corporate influence, national security and the US president’s willingness to listen to intelligence warnings It could be the plot of a spy thriller. One of the most powerful figures in the AI revolution admitted to having…
items.body: I t could be the plot of a spy thriller. One of the most powerful figures in the AI revolution admitted to having an affair with a Chinese businesswomen said to have passed intelligence to Beijing. When Donald Trump was briefed about the Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang’s liaisons with Alice Huang, he took no action. Perhaps he thought only marriage vows had been broken. Or perhaps Mr Trump was willing to overlook the conduct of a friend who championed his unpopular datacentre expansion, whose company donated to his White House ballroom and who echoed his opposition to AI safeguards against expert advice. Nvidia became the cornerstone of AI by supplying brute computing power. As tech giants scrambled for the firm’s graphics processing units (GPUs), Mr Huang sold the picks and shovels for the AI gold rush – and amassed a $160bn fortune.

items.title: Why tech workers are flocking to NYC
items.summary: New York City now has more tech employees than the Bay Area. Here's why workers — and companies — are flocking to the city.
items.body: Erin Sullivan had only visited New York City once before she decided to take a job in the Big Apple. But that visit made a strong impression: "Having the freedom of just hopping on the subway and getting anywhere was so magical for me," she says. "I knew that I wanted to end back up" in the city. After graduating from the University of Oklahoma in 2023 with a computer science degree, Sullivan, 25, landed a role as a software engineer at Bank of America in New York City. The New York metro area is now home to the most tech workers in the country with 394,300 jobs, edging out the San Francisco Bay Area's 375,730 jobs, according to an August report from CBRE, a real estate services and investment firm. Between 2022 and 2025, New York's pool of tech employees grew by over 30,000, while San Francisco's shrank by nearly 24,000 workers.

items.body: Cyberattacks , bomb threats against passenger flights, civil unrest and suspected acts of sabotage across Europe have raised questions about the continent's resilience — and how prepared it is to defend itself against modern security threats. Hackers remotely manipulated refrigeration systems at supermarkets across Europe last week, forcing retailers to discard spoiled food and exposing vulnerabilities in everyday infrastructure. French blood-bank refrigeration systems were subsequently targeted in what appeared to be a similar incident, while a wave of suspected hoax bomb threats disrupted dozens of flights across the continent, forcing diversions and, in some cases, fighter jet escorts. items.body: P hotos That Precede Unfortunate Events: a couple of months back, Donald Trump hosted some of the world’s most powerful tech executives at the White House for a “ Super Intelligence luncheon ”, which by coincidence is also how my mum described her tuna sandwiches in a forlorn attempt to get me to eat them. Winning candidates promised to cut food and healthcare costs, rein in corporations ripping off consumers and workers, curb billionaire power and make the world’s biggest economy better serve the working class. items.body: The government body tasked with keeping the lights on issued a rare call for more electricity supplies on Monday morning due to low wind power generation forecasts across Europe. A notice issued by the National Energy System Operator (Neso) on Sunday night said it faced a “shortfall” of almost 1,400 megawatts in its electricity supply margins from 6am until 11am on Monday. The notice said Neso would need to find extra generation of about 800 megawatts, or the equivalent of a medium-sized gas power plant, within eight hours before a review of power supplies scheduled for 4am. A second “electricity margin notice” issued after the pre-dawn review revealed that Neso’s 11th-hour margin call helped to shrink its shortfall to 500MW. It said that no further contingency power was required but Neso could still call on power plants to generate more than usual between 8am and 11am.

items.title: Weekend trading of Nvidia scandal shines light on new financial products
items.summary: Nvidia scandal shines light growing use of perpetual futures and other trading products
items.body: As news of a potential scandal surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang began to trickle out on Sunday, investors faced a simple question: what could it mean for the stock? One answer could be found in an obscure but growing corner of the markets: perpetual futures. On Sunday at 3 p.m. ET, well before pre-market equity trading had started, a number of traders began placing bearish bets on Nvidia perpetual futures. Specifically, perpetuals on Nvidia traded first, with Hyperliquid's xyz contract slipping to as low as $180.15 on $200 million of volume by 3:30 p.m. E.T. Both equity shares and perps on Nvidia fell below $178 overnight. It traded 7% lower on Monday. Sunday's trading shines a light on a product that is increasingly filling a market void when traditional markets are off-line. In their simplest form, perpetual futures are highly leveraged bets that never expire.

items.title: Nasdaq defies Nvidia impact as Huang faces espionage affair probe
items.summary: The board opens an investigation into Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy
items.body: This is CNBC's Morning Squawk newsletter. Subscribe here to receive future editions in your inbox. Trouble had been brewing, but over the weekend the story broke that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - the so-called 'torchbearer of AI' - has been having an affair with a woman that U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy. The news has sent shockwaves through the markets, with investors scrambling to assess the potential fallout for the AI industry more broadly. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has issued an apology to his family, the company and investors after admitting to an affair with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. The stock is under heavy selling pressure in premarket trading, currently down over 5% and lower by over 6% in Frankfurt. Nvidia's move is keeping Nasdaq futures under pressure, with the index dipping in and out of the red this morning.

items.body: TOKYO/LONDON -- Japanese artificial intelligence developer Sakana AI is preparing for an initial public offering either in Japan or in the U.S. as early as autumn 2027, Nikkei has learned, with a market valuation possibly exceeding Mercari's 680 billion yen ($4.3 billion) to become one of the largest listings for a Japanese startup.

items.title: Crime pays: how Grand Theft Auto became a cultural colossus
items.summary: Ever since it crashed on to PC and consoles in the late 90s, GTA has been tearing up the game-making rulebook. We explore how its cultural references, rebel spirit and sprawling sense of freedom make it a definitive work of art In the 00s, when the Grand Theft Auto developer…
items.body: I n the 00s, when the Grand Theft Auto developer Rockstar Games revealed a new project, video game writers from all over the UK would make the journey to the company’s office in London. They would be ushered one by one into a darkened room to sit facing an enormous TV. There would be a dish of sweets on a low bench in front of them but, in the reverential hush that descended, it was never entirely clear if it was acceptable to eat them. After a few moments, the screen would come to life. Rockstar would sometimes begin its presentation not with footage from its new game, but clips from classic movies. This is the context of what we are making, Rockstar was saying, and that is where we belong. Yet, what’s interesting is that the studio’s ambitions were already straining against its cinematic influences.

items.title: Congress returns with government funding, Pete Hegseth and the debt limit on the agenda
items.summary: Republicans have less than two months left with majorities in both the Senate and the House — and a long list of legislation to take up in the coming weeks.
items.body: The House and Senate are due to return to Washington on Monday with a crowded legislative agenda in the final weeks before the end of the 119th Congress. Congress will need to act quickly to extend government funding , which expires Dec. 11. Lawmakers will need to pass the National Defense Authorization Act, and they may tackle ambitious proposals including a construction permitting package and a bill to regulate name, image and likeness rules in college sports . The work will commence under a new dynamic. Republicans come back to the Capitol diminished after suffering substantial losses in this week's midterms. Democrats swept to a commanding majority in the House with at least 255 seats in the 435-member chamber and could emerge with as many as 56 seats in the Senate.
